new_statements.rule_in_words: Easterday's survey codes Darai as having word stress with fixed (non-lexical, non-weight-sensitive) placement, but does not say on which syllable; LAPSyD, working from the same SIL phonemic summary plus recordings, codes no word stress and reports roughly even prominence except phrase-finally. No primary description seen states a stress position.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in any source seen.
new_statements.domain_note: Easterday's coding is word-level typological coding without page citation; LAPSyD's remark is an auditory impression from recordings and points to phrase-final prominence (phrase-level) rather than word stress. The accessible primary grammar (Dhakal 2011 PhD, Chitwan dialect) treats only intonation (falling for statements/commands/wh-questions, rising for yes-no questions) and is silent on word stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Two dialects are described under dara1250: Kotapish & Kotapish 1973/1975 and Paudyal 2003 describe Tanahun (Pipaltar) Darai; Dhakal 2011/2012 describes Chitwan (Pidrahani) Darai. Dhakal notes the dialects differ in 'accent' (sociolinguistic sense) and verb agreement. Easterday's and LAPSyD's codings both rest mainly on the Tanahun-based SIL phonemic summary.
